stem: A client taking oral capecitabine at home realizes a scheduled dose was missed. Which instruction should the nurse reinforce?

options.A: Skip the missed dose and take the next dose at the usual scheduled time.
options.B: Take the missed dose as soon as it is remembered, even if the next dose is due soon.
options.C: Take two doses at the next scheduled time to replace the dose that was missed.
options.D: Stop capecitabine permanently after any missed dose and discard the remaining tablets.

rationale: Current capecitabine prescribing information instructs patients not to replace a missed dose; they should continue with the next planned dose at the scheduled time. The label also instructs patients not to take an additional dose after vomiting. Doubling or independently changing the regimen can increase medication risk and is not recommended.
educational_objective: Teach the correct response to a missed oral capecitabine dose: do not replace or double it; resume with the next scheduled dose.
source_organization: DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_document_title: CAPECITABINE tablets, for oral use — Full Prescribing Information
source_locator: Section 2.6 Dosage Modifications for Adverse Reactions and Section 2.8 Administration; Patient Information — How should I take capecitabine tablets?
source_claim_supported: The current capecitabine label states not to replace missed doses and to resume with the next planned dosage; it also states not to take an additional dose after vomiting and to continue with the next scheduled dose.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication-related nursing activity statements/content
blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — medication administration and client education
correction_summary: Rebuilt a broad oral-chemotherapy adherence item into a capecitabine-specific missed-dose teaching item. Replaced the generic ONS homepage source with a current July 2026 DailyMed prescribing label and exact administration locator. Removed vague class-wide claims and created one clinically actionable, uniquely correct instruction.
audit_findings: Original item was too broad to verify across all oral antineoplastic agents because adherence, food, handling, and missed-dose instructions are drug-specific.
Current capecitabine labeling directly states that a missed dose should not be replaced and the next scheduled dose should be taken as planned.
The rebuilt item avoids unsupported class-wide assertions and does not permit client-directed dose adjustment.
Distractors are plausible medication-error patterns but conflict directly with the label.
Independent adversarial review found no ambiguity, second answer, cueing, unsupported precision, or unresolved source conflict.
